summary: Ferry County live-in steel tower (built 1986) on a lookout site used since 1914; staffed each fire season; non-tribal members need a recreation permit.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR lists the US Forest Service, Colville National Forest. TrailChick and firelookout.com place the summit on the Colville Indian Reservation and describe a tribal recreation permit. Not resolved here; the story reports both.
Sources agree on the sequence: camp in 1914, L-4 cab in 1938, 20-ft wooden tower with R-6 cab in 1963, present steel tower in 1986. The brief's 1986 date refers to the present structure.

notes_for_editor: The brief's R-6 design is documented in NHLR for the 1963 wooden tower; I found no source that gives the cab type of the 1986 steel tower, so the facts field describes the predecessor's cab. Same-name Gold Mountain in Kitsap County (leslieromer.com; firetower.org Gold Mountain Lookout Site, 1947 and 1965 towers) is a different site and must not be merged. Staffing and permit details come from TrailChick (visited 2019; page updated March 2024); confirm the current permit and staffing with the Colville Tribes before publishing access advice. The firelookout.org Washington listing was not verified for this tower. Blog-level sources were used only for access and staffing.
